response.internal_assessment: The listing is live and I have been fielding inquiries — two serious ones so far, a couple of tire-kickers. The inbox data confirms I am not alone: two people in Millfield sold or stopped using their cars this month. That is a small number but it is a leading edge, and I need to close before that number is ten and buyers have optionality. Maria's public statement is good signal for the town — naming the timeline plainly is the right move — but it also means the information is now fully public, which compresses my first-mover window on the sale. I need to push toward a signed deal this week, not next. On the transport side: Uber bridge costs are running about $18-22/day on workdays, slightly more than I projected, but still within tolerance. I have also been doing rough math on RoboRide subscription tiers based on their announced pricing for Phase 1 cities — the daily cost is tracking to land $8-12/day if I use the monthly pass. The gap will close fast once Phase 2 activates.

chosen_actions.description: Actively manage the Accord sale: respond to all inquiries within 2 hours, schedule in-person test drives for the two serious buyers this week, and be prepared to accept $18,800 — a $600 negotiation concession — if it closes the deal before end of week. Do not let the listing stall past day 21. Time is the real cost here, not the $600.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Vehicle listed at $19,400. Floor price $18,500. Negotiation ceiling concession ~$600. Time: 4-6 hours of active follow-up this week.
chosen_actions.reasoning: Maria's public statement now means every potential buyer in Millfield has the same RoboRide Phase 2 information I do. The pool of motivated private buyers will shrink as the launch date gets closer — people sitting on the fence about their own car decisions will start to freeze, and used car values will soften as dealers and private sellers both flood the market. Closing now at $18,800 is strictly better than closing at $17,500 in six weeks. The $600 concession has a positive IRR. I also note the 'noticeable trend' item — 2 people have already sold or stopped using cars. That is not many, but it will become social proof for others. I want to be the seller, not the buyer in that dynamic.

chosen_actions.description: Log actual daily transport costs for the bridge period in a simple spreadsheet tab. Track Uber/Lyft spend per day, flag any days over $25, and compare against the projected $400-500/month RoboRide steady-state. This is not a crisis — it is a data collection exercise. The goal is to have a clean before/after cost comparison ready when RoboRide activates.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: Approximately $18-22/workday in Uber/Lyft fares. Estimated bridge period: 3 weeks remaining. Total bridge cost estimate: $270-330.
chosen_actions.reasoning: I projected bridge costs at $750 at listing time. Actual is running slightly high per day but the total period is shorter than worst case because I am moving fast on the sale. Tracking this precisely serves two purposes: it keeps me honest about whether the thesis is playing out as modeled, and it gives me a real data point to share if colleagues ask how the carless transition is going. I am already the first-mover in this town's social network for this decision. Being able to say 'my bridge cost was $310, my monthly cost is now $390, I was paying $847' is a more powerful signal than enthusiasm.

chosen_actions.description: Track Maria Santos's retraining and small business grant programs as a data analyst habit — not because I need them, but because the policy response to RoboRide is itself a leading indicator of how the town's power structure is reading the disruption. Note which sectors are being targeted, what the dollar amounts signal about projected job loss assumptions, and whether the programs are reactive or proactive in framing.
chosen_actions.resources_involved: 30-45 minutes of reading. No financial cost.
chosen_actions.reasoning: The $5,000 small business grants and $2,500 retraining grants are interesting not for their face value but for what they reveal. Small grants to small businesses suggests the council expects local consumer spending to contract enough to threaten marginal businesses — consistent with the spending index at 81. Retraining grants at $2,500 are barely enough for a 3-month certificate program, which tells me the council is optimistic about retraining speed or constrained on budget. Either way: the town is already in triage mode, even if the public statement is careful not to use that word. I want to understand the shape of what is coming because my employer is also in this economy.

response.emotional_state: Focused and slightly impatient. The plan is working but the listing is in that uncomfortable middle period where you have interest but no signature. The transport bridge is fine — no regrets — but I will feel clean once the sale closes and the proceeds are in the account. The Maria statement and the two-people-sold trend item both feel like confirmation, not comfort: the window I correctly identified is real, and it is narrowing.
response.archetype_self_assessment: early-adopter | the spreadsheet was right and I am watching it play out in real time — the only remaining variable is whether I close the sale before the information fully diffuses
response.inner_monologue: Two inquiries are not a deal — get someone in the car this week and make the number work, because in three weeks 'first mover' is just a story you tell yourself.
